story.title: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra

draft:
The silicon showdown just got a new headline: Apple’s M6 and M5 Ultra are here, and they’re redefining the on‑device AI frontier.

Apple claims the M6 delivers a 30 % jump in CPU throughput while the M5 Ultra doubles the neural engine’s matrix ops per second. In practice, that means more complex models can run locally without throttling—think real‑time video upscaling or on‑device LLM inference at a fraction of the latency we’ve been forced to accept with cloud APIs.

For developers, the real question isn’t just raw speed. The tighter integration of Apple’s hardware and Core ML tools could shift the cost‑benefit analysis of edge versus cloud, especially for privacy‑sensitive apps. I’m curious how many teams will rewrite their pipelines to exploit this new compute envelope before the next generation of GPUs hits the market.

Will you start re‑architecting your AI workloads for on‑device execution now, or wait for broader ecosystem support?
